name: How do you know if a side addition is better than an interior remodel?

mainEntity.name: How do you know if a side addition is better than an interior remodel?
mainEntity.text: How do you know if a side addition is better than an interior remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: A side addition is usually better than an interior remodel when the main problem is lack of square footage rather than poor layout alone. If rooms are cramped, hallways are too narrow, or the home needs an additional bedroom, larger kitchen, or expanded living area, an addition may solve the issue more completely than reshuffling existing walls. Interior remodels work best when the home already has enough space but the flow is inefficient. Side additions become attractive when there is usable side-yard width and the owner wants to add function without sacrificing the backyard. The tradeoff is cost and complexity: additions are usually more expensive because they involve foundation, framing, roof tie-in, and permit review. A good decision starts with a space plan showing what can be fixed internally and what can only be solved by adding area. The best option is the one that gives the most practical improvement for the money while fitting the lot and the long-term goals for the property.
acceptedAnswer.description: A side addition is better when the existing floor plan cannot be fixed by reconfiguring interior space alone. If the home needs more square footage, better room proportions, or a new functional zone, adding space is usually more effective than moving walls.
